name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Sense organs of frog and their sensory modalities

questiontext.text:
Match the sense organs of frog in List I with their corresponding sensory functions in List II:

List I List II
A. Sensory papillaeI. Smell
B. Taste budsII. Touch
C. Nasal epitheliumIII. Hearing and balancing
D. Tympanum with internal earIV. Taste

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Determine the sensory function of sensory papillae.
In frogs, sensory papillae are skin receptors that act as the organs of touch. Therefore, sensory papillae match with touch.

Step 2: Determine the sensory function of taste buds.
Taste buds are chemical receptors located within the buccal cavity that function as the organs of taste. Therefore, taste buds match with taste.

Step 3: Determine the sensory function of nasal epithelium.
The nasal epithelium lines the olfactory chambers and functions as the organ of smell. Therefore, nasal epithelium matches with smell.

Step 4: Determine the sensory function of tympanum with internal ear.
The tympanum is visible externally and works in conjunction with the internal ear to receive acoustic vibrations and maintain equilibrium, serving as the organ of hearing and balancing. Therefore, tympanum with internal ear matches with hearing and balancing.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs gives: Sensory papillae – Touch; Taste buds – Taste; Nasal epithelium – Smell; Tympanum with internal ear – Hearing and balancing. Thus, the correct matching is A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Morphological structures of frog and their functions

questiontext.text:
Match the external morphological structures of frog in List I with their descriptions or functions in List II:

List I List II
A. Nictitating membraneI. Helps in swimming in water
B. Webbed feetII. Produce sound in male frogs
C. Copulatory padIII. Protects bulged eyes while in water
D. Vocal sacsIV. Present on the first digit of male forelimbs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the role of the nictitating membrane.
Frogs have bulged eyes covered by a transparent nictitating membrane that provides physical protection while the animal is submerged in water. Therefore, nictitating membrane matches with protecting bulged eyes while in water.

Step 2: Identify the role of webbed feet.
The hind limbs end in five digits joined by webs of skin (webbed digits), which function as paddles to aid swimming. Therefore, webbed feet match with helping in swimming in water.

Step 3: Identify the nature and position of copulatory pad.
Frogs show sexual dimorphism; male frogs possess a copulatory pad on the first digit of each forelimb, which is completely absent in females. Therefore, copulatory pad matches with being present on the first digit of male forelimbs.

Step 4: Identify the role of vocal sacs.
Male frogs possess a pair of sound-producing vocal sacs beneath the throat that amplify croaking to attract mates. Therefore, vocal sacs match with producing sound in male frogs.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Assembling the derived pairs: Nictitating membrane – Protects bulged eyes while in water; Webbed feet – Helps in swimming in water; Copulatory pad – Present on the first digit of male forelimbs; Vocal sacs – Produce sound in male frogs. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Brain regions of frog and their constituent structures

questiontext.text:
Match the regions of the central nervous system of frog in List I with their constituent structures or characteristics in List II:

List I List II
A. ForebrainI. Olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, and unpaired diencephalon
B. MidbrainII. Passes through foramen magnum to continue into spinal cord
C. HindbrainIII. Characterised by a pair of optic lobes
D. Medulla oblongataIV. Consists of cerebellum and medulla oblongata

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the anatomical parts of the forebrain.
In frogs, the brain is enclosed within the cranium. The forebrain consists of olfactory lobes anteriorly, followed by paired cerebral hemispheres and an unpaired diencephalon. Therefore, forebrain matches with olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, and unpaired diencephalon.

Step 2: Identify the anatomical parts of the midbrain.
The midbrain of frog is prominently characterised by a pair of dorsolateral optic lobes. Therefore, midbrain matches with being characterised by a pair of optic lobes.

Step 3: Identify the components of the hindbrain.
The hindbrain of frog is composed of two distinct regions: a small transverse cerebellum and a posterior medulla oblongata. Therefore, hindbrain matches with consisting of cerebellum and medulla oblongata.

Step 4: Trace the continuation of the medulla oblongata.
The medulla oblongata emerges out of the cranial cavity through the large posterior opening called the foramen magnum and continues posteriorly as the spinal cord inside the vertebral column. Therefore, medulla oblongata matches with passing through the foramen magnum to continue into spinal cord.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Forebrain – Olfactory lobes, paired cerebral hemispheres, and unpaired diencephalon; Midbrain – Characterised by a pair of optic lobes; Hindbrain – Consists of cerebellum and medulla oblongata; Medulla oblongata – Passes through foramen magnum to continue into spinal cord. Thus, the correct matching is A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Vascular structures of frog and their anatomical roles

questiontext.text:
Match the circulatory structures of frog in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. Sinus venosusI. Sac-like structure on ventral side of heart opening from ventricle
B. Conus arteriosusII. Venous connection between kidney and lower parts of body
C. Hepatic portal systemIII. Triangular structure joining right atrium and receiving venae cavae
D. Renal portal systemIV. Venous connection between liver and intestine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Characterize the sinus venosus.
The sinus venosus is a triangular chamber situated on the dorsal side of the frog heart that joins the right atrium and receives deoxygenated blood through the major veins called venae cavae. Therefore, sinus venosus matches with triangular structure joining right atrium and receiving venae cavae.

Step 2: Characterize the conus arteriosus.
The muscular ventricle pumps blood out into a funnel- or sac-like conus arteriosus located on the ventral surface of the heart, which then bifurcates into aortic trunks. Therefore, conus arteriosus matches with sac-like structure on ventral side of heart opening from ventricle.

Step 3: Characterize the hepatic portal system.
The hepatic portal system represents a specialised venous pathway that collects blood from the alimentary canal (intestine) and delivers it to the liver before returning to the heart. Therefore, hepatic portal system matches with venous connection between liver and intestine.

Step 4: Characterize the renal portal system.
The renal portal system is a specialised venous arrangement that transports venous blood from the hind limbs and lower pelvic regions directly to the kidneys. Therefore, renal portal system matches with venous connection between kidney and lower parts of body.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Synthesizing the matches: Sinus venosus – Triangular structure joining right atrium and receiving venae cavae; Conus arteriosus – Sac-like structure on ventral side of heart opening from ventricle; Hepatic portal system – Venous connection between liver and intestine; Renal portal system – Venous connection between kidney and lower parts of body. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Digestive secretions of frog and their specific actions

questiontext.text:
Match the secretions and substances of frog in List I with their functions or roles in List II:

List I List II
A. BileI. Digestion of carbohydrates and proteins
B. Gastric juice and HClII. Keeps skin smooth, moist, and slippery
C. Pancreatic juiceIII. Emulsification of dietary fats
D. MucusIV. Breakdown of food to produce chyme in stomach

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the role of bile.
Bile is synthesized by the liver, stored in the gall bladder, and released into the duodenum via the common bile duct to emulsify large fat globules. Therefore, bile matches with emulsification of dietary fats.

Step 2: Identify the role of gastric juice and hydrochloric acid.
Gastric juice and HCl are secreted by the walls of the stomach, initiating protein breakdown and reducing ingested food into a semi-liquid mass known as chyme. Therefore, gastric juice and HCl match with breakdown of food to produce chyme in stomach.

Step 3: Identify the role of pancreatic juice.
Pancreatic juice is produced by the pancreas and delivered to the duodenum; it contains digestive enzymes responsible for digesting carbohydrates and proteins. Therefore, pancreatic juice matches with digestion of carbohydrates and proteins.

Step 4: Identify the role of mucus.
Mucus is continuously secreted by cutaneous glands in the skin, keeping it moist, smooth, and slippery to facilitate cutaneous respiration and reduce friction. Therefore, mucus matches with keeping skin smooth, moist, and slippery.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Bile – Emulsification of dietary fats; Gastric juice and HCl – Breakdown of food to produce chyme in stomach; Pancreatic juice – Digestion of carbohydrates and proteins; Mucus – Keeps skin smooth, moist, and slippery. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Male reproductive structures of frog and their features

questiontext.text:
Match the structures of the male urinogenital system of frog in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. MesorchiumI. 10 to 12 fine ducts emerging from testes and entering kidneys
B. Vasa efferentiaII. Ducts carrying both urine and spermatozoa to cloaca
C. Bidder's canalIII. Double fold of peritoneum anchoring testes to upper kidneys
D. Male uretersIV. Longitudinal canal in kidney receiving vasa efferentia

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the role and structure of the mesorchium.
In male frogs, the pair of yellowish ovoid testes is suspended and adhered to the antero-dorsal surface of the kidneys by a specialized double fold of peritoneum called the mesorchium. Therefore, mesorchium matches with double fold of peritoneum anchoring testes to upper kidneys.

Step 2: Identify the origin and number of vasa efferentia.
There are 10 to 12 vasa efferentia that emerge from each testis, penetrate the medial border of the kidney, and communicate internally. Therefore, vasa efferentia matches with 10 to 12 fine ducts emerging from testes and entering kidneys.

Step 3: Trace the location of Bidder's canal.
Inside the kidney of a male frog, the vasa efferentia open directly into a longitudinal duct known as Bidder's canal, which then connects with the ureter. Therefore, Bidder's canal matches with longitudinal canal in kidney receiving vasa efferentia.

Step 4: Characterize the male ureters.
In male frogs, because the ureters convey both urine from the kidneys and spermatozoa from Bidder's canal into the cloaca, they function as urinogenital ducts. Therefore, male ureters match with ducts carrying both urine and spermatozoa to cloaca.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Mesorchium – Double fold of peritoneum anchoring testes to upper kidneys; Vasa efferentia – 10 to 12 fine ducts emerging from testes and entering kidneys; Bidder's canal – Longitudinal canal in kidney receiving vasa efferentia; Male ureters – Ducts carrying both urine and spermatozoa to cloaca. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Physiological and ecological adaptations of Indian frog

questiontext.text:
Match the biological terms related to frog adaptations in List I with their descriptions in List II:

List I List II
A. PoikilothermyI. Body temperature fluctuates with ambient environmental temperature
B. CamouflageII. Summer sleep in deep burrows during peak hot periods
C. AestivationIII. Transformation of larval tadpole into an adult frog
D. MetamorphosisIV. Ability to change skin colour to blend into surroundings and evade predators

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define poikilothermy in frogs.
Frogs are cold-blooded animals or poikilotherms because they lack intrinsic thermoregulation and their core body temperature fluctuates according to the temperature of the surrounding environment. Therefore, poikilothermy matches with body temperature fluctuates with ambient environmental temperature.

Step 2: Define camouflage in frogs.
Frogs exhibit camouflage (mimicry/protective coloration) by altering skin pigmentation to blend in with green grasses or dry terrain, concealing them from predators. Therefore, camouflage matches with ability to change skin colour to blend into surroundings and evade predators.

Step 3: Define aestivation in frogs.
During peak summer heat and drought, frogs take refuge deep in moist burrows to minimize thermal stress and desiccation, a dormancy period termed summer sleep or aestivation. Therefore, aestivation matches with summer sleep in deep burrows during peak hot periods.

Step 4: Define metamorphosis in frogs.
Development in frogs involves an indirect life cycle where the aquatic, tailed, gill-bearing tadpole undergoes drastic anatomical remodeling to produce the terrestrial adult frog. Therefore, metamorphosis matches with transformation of larval tadpole into an adult frog.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Pairing each concept: Poikilothermy – Body temperature fluctuates with ambient environmental temperature; Camouflage – Ability to change skin colour to blend into surroundings and evade predators; Aestivation – Summer sleep in deep burrows during peak hot periods; Metamorphosis – Transformation of larval tadpole into an adult frog. Thus, the correct matching is A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Body fluids and excretory structures in frog

questiontext.text:
Match the circulatory and excretory components of frog in List I with their defining characteristics in List II:

List I List II
A. Erythrocytes (RBCs)I. Structural and functional microscopic units of the kidney
B. LymphII. Circulating body fluid that lacks RBCs and a few blood proteins
C. Uriniferous tubulesIII. Thin-walled bilobed sac situated ventral to the rectum
D. Urinary bladderIV. Nucleated oval blood cells containing haemoglobin pigment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the erythrocytes of frog.
Unlike non-nucleated human red blood cells, the erythrocytes of frogs are biconvex, oval, nucleated, and contain the respiratory pigment haemoglobin. Therefore, erythrocytes (RBCs) match with nucleated oval blood cells containing haemoglobin pigment.

Step 2: Analyze the composition of lymph in frog.
The lymphatic system of frog contains lymph, lymph channels, and lymph nodes. Lymph is distinct from blood because it completely lacks erythrocytes (RBCs) and has lower concentrations of specific plasma proteins. Therefore, lymph matches with circulating body fluid that lacks RBCs and a few blood proteins.

Step 3: Analyze the functional units of the frog kidney.
Each dark-red, bean-like kidney is composed of thousands of structural and functional excretory units termed uriniferous tubules or nephrons. Therefore, uriniferous tubules match with structural and functional microscopic units of the kidney.

Step 4: Analyze the urinary bladder of frog.
In frogs, the urinary bladder is a thin-walled, distensible sac positioned ventrally with respect to the rectum that discharges its contents directly into the cloaca. Therefore, urinary bladder matches with thin-walled bilobed sac situated ventral to the rectum.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Synthesizing the matches: Erythrocytes (RBCs) – Nucleated oval blood cells containing haemoglobin pigment; Lymph – Circulating body fluid that lacks RBCs and a few blood proteins; Uriniferous tubules – Structural and functional microscopic units of the kidney; Urinary bladder – Thin-walled bilobed sac situated ventral to the rectum. Thus, the correct matching is A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Urinogenital structures in male and female frogs

questiontext.text:
Match the urinogenital organs of frog in List I with their anatomical connections or routes in List II:

List I List II
A. Female uretersI. Emerge from kidneys to carry both urine and spermatozoa into the cloaca
B. Male uretersII. Small median chamber receiving excretory, digestive, and genital outputs
C. Female ovariesIII. Transport only urine and open into the cloaca independently of oviducts
D. CloacaIV. Situated near the kidneys without any functional connection with them

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluate the female ureters.
In female frogs, the ureters conduct only urine from the kidneys and empty directly into the cloaca without merging with the genital system; the oviducts open into the cloaca through separate apertures. Therefore, female ureters match with transport only urine and open into the cloaca independently of oviducts.

Step 2: Evaluate the male ureters.
In male frogs, the ureters receive spermatozoa from Bidder's canal inside the kidneys and carry both urinary waste and gametes to the cloaca, thus functioning as urinogenital ducts. Therefore, male ureters match with emerge from kidneys to carry both urine and spermatozoa into the cloaca.

Step 3: Evaluate the anatomical relationship of female ovaries.
The pair of lobulated ovaries in female frogs is situated near the kidneys, but unlike the male testes, there is no structural or functional duct connection between the ovaries and the kidneys. Therefore, female ovaries match with situated near the kidneys without any functional connection with them.

Step 4: Evaluate the role of the cloaca.
The cloaca is a small, common median terminal chamber that receives undigested faecal matter from the rectum, urine from the ureters/urinary bladder, and gametes from the reproductive tract before discharging them to the exterior via the cloacal aperture. Therefore, cloaca matches with small median chamber receiving excretory, digestive, and genital outputs.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Female ureters – Transport only urine and open into the cloaca independently of oviducts; Male ureters – Emerge from kidneys to carry both urine and spermatozoa into the cloaca; Female ovaries – Situated near the kidneys without any functional connection with them; Cloaca – Small median chamber receiving excretory, digestive, and genital outputs. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STRUCTURAL_ORGANISATION_IN_ANIMALS_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Organisation of nervous system and sense organs

questiontext.text:
Match the neural and sensory divisions of frog in List I with their constituents in List II:

List I List II
A. Central nervous systemI. Sensory papillae, taste buds, and nasal epithelium
B. Peripheral nervous systemII. Ten pairs of cranial nerves and paired spinal nerves
C. Well-organised sense organsIII. Brain protected in cranium and spinal cord in vertebral column
D. Cellular aggregations around nerve endingsIV. Spherical eyes situated in orbits and internal ears

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the constituents of the central nervous system.
The central nervous system of frog consists of the brain, enclosed inside the bony brain box or cranium, and the spinal cord, enclosed within the vertebral column. Therefore, central nervous system matches with brain protected in cranium and spinal cord in vertebral column.

Step 2: Identify the constituents of the peripheral nervous system.
The peripheral nervous system connects the central axis to body parts and is composed of ten pairs of cranial nerves emerging from the brain along with pairs of spinal nerves originating from the spinal cord. Therefore, peripheral nervous system matches with ten pairs of cranial nerves and paired spinal nerves.

Step 3: Distinguish the well-organised sense organs of frog.
Among the five sensory modalities present in frog, the eyes (spherical simple eyes situated in skull orbits) and internal ears (responsible for hearing and equilibrium) are anatomically complex, well-organised organs. Therefore, well-organised sense organs matches with spherical eyes situated in orbits and internal ears.

Step 4: Distinguish the simpler sensory receptor aggregations.
Unlike eyes and ears, the organs of touch (sensory papillae), taste (taste buds), and smell (nasal epithelium) are non-encapsulated, simple cellular aggregations organized around terminal nerve endings. Therefore, cellular aggregations around nerve endings matches with sensory papillae, taste buds, and nasal epithelium.

Step 5: Final conclusion and answer matching.
Combining these pairs: Central nervous system – Brain protected in cranium and spinal cord in vertebral column; Peripheral nervous system – Ten pairs of cranial nerves and paired spinal nerves; Well-organised sense organs – Spherical eyes situated in orbits and internal ears; Cellular aggregations around nerve endings – Sensory papillae, taste buds, and nasal epithelium. Thus, the correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.
